title: Trajectories of resilience and dysfunction following potential trauma: A review and statistical evaluation
authors: Galatzer-Levy, Huang and Bonanno (2018), Clinical Psychology Review 63:41-55, doi 10.1016/j.cpr.2018.05.008
universe: People followed after a potentially traumatic event (bereavement, injury, disaster, combat and others)
geography: Studies from several countries; no place breakdown
limits: Symptom trajectories, not actions: resilience means stable healthy functioning, which the drives engine's carry-on response stands for, but a resilient person may still take up a cause. All event types pooled; bereavement alone is not separated in the abstract.
quote: The resilience trajectory was the modal response across studies (average of 65.7% across populations, 95% CI [0.616, 0.698]), followed in prevalence by recovery (20.8% [0.162, 0.258]), chronicity (10.6%, [0.086, 0.127]), and delayed onset (8.9% [0.053, 0.133]).
use: SG-P10-response-model: the band the share of people who carry on after a loss is reported against (scripts/research/people-year.ts); the builder item people-drives-responses-against-research-bands calibrates the response pressures to it.
